content.title: Men’s March Madness Selection Sunday live updates and reaction: Duke, Arizona, Michigan, Florida grab No. 1 seeds in NCAA Tournament
content.text: The men's NCAA Tournament bracket is set as we head into March Madness Cameron Boozer's Duke team is the No. 1 overall seed in the NCAA Tournament. Getty ImagesMen's March Madness bracket is setThe men’s NCAA Tournament field is complete as we head into March Madness. Duke, Arizona, Michigan and Florida have been unveiled as the No. 1 seeds. Miami (OH) is in as an at-large team after a 31-1 season. The SEC has 10 teams in the field, followed by the Big Ten with nine and the ACC and Big 12 with eight each.The games begin on Tuesday and Wednesday with the First Four, followed by the first round on Thursday and Friday. First time since 2017, the MWC gets only one team in the NCAAT.— Aztec Analytics (@AztecAnalytics) March 15, 2026 The Keith Gill interview is yet another reminder how much more consistent and methodical the hoops selection process is than football. And he can actually articulate their reasoning, unlike those Tuesday night CFP shows.Your reactions to the 68-team field Getty ImagesFrank D.: How can UConn be a #2 and St. John's a number #5?Aberylyman: Florida has way too many losses to be a 1 seed. As usual, they made sure that SEC schools have an advantage at every turn.Chris S.: I don’t think they did Duke any favors, despite making them the #1 overall seed. A lot of talented teams in that region.Matt U.: Thank the LORD Auburn didn’t make it. I’ve never heard such a fuss from such an average team!Alex W.: It would have killed the tourney to just give Miami (Ohio) a free and clear bid, instead of the First Four?Props to Sun Belt commissioner Keith Gill for a good job explaining the selections and decisions behind them. Clear and concise. Football could really use that.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementTo Joe's and Devon's points, I wonder if the relative controversy of the College Football Playoff field (and extended backlash to it) helped diminish the controversy of this field once Miami (Ohio) was confirmed to be in. Also, it's obviously a lot harder for non-invested fans to empathize when a team left "out" finished 17-16. And, yes, credit to Bruce Pearl for not making a huge scene over Auburn being that team left out.Big day for the ACC Also, today is a huge win for the ACC, which doubled its number of teams in the field compared to just four last season. Yes, two of those (NC State and SMU) are in Dayton in the First Four, but the league's increased investment worked out how commissioner Jim Phillips hoped it would. Huge kudos to Phillips for pushing ACC programs to spend in men's basketball, a much-needed modernization after several down years for the historic conference.Our college basketball men's Big Board is up!
